sections.title: Adding the batch and saving
sections.what: Builds the new ledger entry after the last batch, rejects duplicates, confirms the input files are in the repo, then saves the ledger and prints a confirmation line.
sections.why: Likely reason: duplicate checks stop one approved run from being loaded twice, and the order number keeps batches in sequence.
sections.watch_out: The duplicate check only catches exact matches on batch name or plan digest, and the save has no undo.

summary: Adds one approved, committed research batch to an industry's replay ledger so that it loads into the main database after the merge.
purpose: A replay ledger is a running list of approved batches. Registering a batch here puts it in the list in order, so the later replay script can load it.
why: The header says to run this right after the commit. Keeping an ordered ledger means batches load in the same order they were approved.
how: It reads the folder and commit report from the command line, checks the report exists, and picks the importer type and industry. It builds a new entry with the next order number, rejects a duplicate batch name or plan digest, checks the input files are in the repo, then appends the entry and saves the ledger.
inputs: Command line arguments: the ledger folder, the commit report path, and optional --importer, --batch and --note values. It also reads the industry manifest and the existing replay ledger file.
outputs: An updated replay-ledger.json file in the folder, and one confirmation line naming the batch, its order and its row count.
risks: The script writes a ledger file in the repo, and it has no undo. A wrong importer or folder will place the batch in the wrong ledger.
debug: Error messages name the problem: no such report means the path is wrong; already in the ledger means a duplicate name or digest; not in the repo means the input files must be committed first; a record industry mismatch means the ledger and manifest disagree.
